elements.title: Fortescue Cuming (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Fortescue Cuming (pictured) gave a "reasonably sane" account of Kentucky after his travels in 1807?

elements.title: Cueyamil railway station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that six people died in floods next to the Cueyamil railway station, on an avenue where residents had previously reported problems with the drainage system?

elements.title: Albert Ham (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that organist and choirmaster Albert Ham banned women from singing in the choir of the Cathedral Church of St. James for more than 30 years?

elements.title: cockchafers (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Nikola Tesla recalled harnessing the power of four cockchafers as one of his first "inventions" as a child?

elements.title: a video game modder (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that a video game modder put an entire video game console inside a video game cartridge?

elements.title: Razis threw his entrails at enemy soldiers (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that, when Razis threw his entrails at enemy soldiers, it implied their defeat despite the act resulting in his death?

elements.title: Chow Shu-kai (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Chow Shu-kai led Taiwan's delegation out of the United Nations General Assembly in 1971 before the assembly voted on China's representation at the UN?

elements.title: Hollywood Walk of Fame (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the Apollo 11 astronauts were added to the Hollywood Walk of Fame for their contributions to the television industry?

elements.title: Kate Tolo (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Kate Tolo "could not be more proud" of her boyfriend for tweeting about her vagina?
